bull.t: Rapid Revenue Growth And Improving Adjusted Profitability
bull.b: Exceptional revenue growth demonstrates strong adoption of Nebius’s AI cloud offering, while the swing to substantial adjusted EBITDA indicates improving operating leverage. If demand and capacity expansion remain aligned, this combination can support a more durable earnings base over the next several quarters.

Longer-term contracts, higher pricing and substantial upfront payments improve revenue visibility and reduce the amount of internally funded capital required for expansion. This customer commitment also supports liquidity and can make capacity investment more economically durable as the platform scales.

Control over infrastructure, hardware deployment and software can improve cost efficiency, utilization and service integration compared with a less coordinated offering. Greater ownership of the stack may support sustained margins and product differentiation as AI workloads become more demanding.

bear.b: Positive net income has not yet translated into consistent operating profitability, leaving earnings quality dependent on factors outside the core business. Persistently negative EBIT and EBITDA could constrain reinvestment capacity and make future results more sensitive to execution and expansion timing.

The infrastructure build-out requires substantial cash spending that currently exceeds operating inflows, creating a continuing funding requirement. If large investment outlays persist or capacity takes longer to generate revenue, cash conversion may remain weak and financial flexibility could be pressured.

bear.t: Capacity Deployment Delays Are Shifting Revenue
bear.b: Delays in bringing contracted capacity online can defer revenue even when customer demand remains strong, while fixed site costs may begin before utilization. Repeated timing slippage could slow the conversion of contracted demand into reported growth and complicate margin delivery.
